attributes.probed_form: TWO probes, both reverted; the tree is byte-identical to HEAD. (1) EXPLICIT DECLARED BASE - the v1 record's own mandated axis, and it is REFUTED: `WorldInfo* wi;` inserted as the THIRD declaration (after `u8* data_off; u8* track_off;` and before `s32* count;`), with `wi = &gWorldInfo;` at the top of the guarded block and `count = &wi->nworldanims; header = (s32*)wi->animheader;` plus `(u8*)wi->worldanims` and `(u8*)wi->animdata` in the loop body. The position was chosen deliberately: retail's descending order is data_off(r31), track_off(r30), base(r29), count(r28), i(r27), anim_base(r26), which is EXACTLY our declaration list with the base inserted third - so if the base ranked as a declared local this form would have closed the function outright. 13 words, and the aligned view over 0x5c:0x95 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD: the base stayed in r31 and the offsets stayed in r29/r28. NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, decisive at one. (2) INTEGER BASE WEB: `u32 wi;` with `wi = (u32)&gWorldInfo; count = (s32*)(wi + 144); header = *(s32**)(wi + 148);` and the loop reading `*(u8**)(wi + 140)` and `*(u8**)(wi + 152)`. REGRESSED 13 -> 20 words with 12 mnemonic divergences at 63/63: the `addi r28,r31,144` that computes `count` sank into the guard block at +0x80 and the three `li 0` initialisers re-ordered around it, so re-typing the base does not demote it from the address block, it only breaks the schedule that was already correct.
attributes.residual: The rule stays. THE MECHANISM is unchanged from v1 and is confirmed word-for-word: four values live in r28-r31 and both streams define them in the same order and at the same offsets - the CSE'd `&gWorldInfo` base (+0x60 target `addi r29,r3,0` against ours `addi r31,r3,0`), the loop-limit address base+144 (+0x64 target `addi r28,r29,144` against ours `addi r30,r31,144`), the 160-stride offset (+0x8c target `li r31,0` against ours `li r29,0`) and the 16-stride offset (+0x90 target `li r30,0` against ours `li r28,0`), with i (r27) and anim_base (r26) agreeing everywhere. WHAT THIS PASS ADDS: v1 capped on the declaration-ORDER axis and left the ADDRESS-TEMP axis explicitly undenied as the next lane's step 1. That axis has now been run in both of its available directions and both are dead. Declaring the base as a first-class local of the correct type, positioned exactly where retail's register order says it belongs, produces byte-identical code; re-typing it as an integer keeps it in the address block and costs 7 words plus 12 mnemonic divergences. Together with `count` - a declared `s32*` that our build also puts in the address block at r30 - this establishes that the block boundary is a property of the VALUE (an address of a global) and is not addressable through declaration, position, or declared type. Also confirmed against the target this run: retail re-loads gWorldInfo.worldanims and gWorldInfo.animdata inside the loop at +0xac and +0xc0, so the offset-accumulator source shape is the faithful one and a walking-pointer rewrite would be wrong on count, not merely on colour.

It does NOT deny a pragma lever, and it does not deny the loop-depth/use-density axis named in `hypothesis`, which was not tried.

held_fixed: The function signature, the statement ORDER, the loop shape, the offset-accumulator idiom (`data_off`/`track_off` walked as u8* from NULL and cast to u32 at each use) and the declaration list's relative order were held constant across both probes. Each varied exactly one thing: whether the gWorldInfo base is an anonymous CSE temp or an explicitly declared local of pointer type; and then the base web's TYPE CLASS, pointer versus integer.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Check whether retail re-loads the two gWorldInfo fields inside the loop or hoists them. If retail hoists them, the base web is not loop-resident at all and the density reading is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03 from the aligned view over 0xac:0xe4: retail emits `lwz r0,140(r29)` at +0xac and `lwz r0,152(r29)` at +0xc0, both INSIDE the loop body, and we emit the identical pair off r31 - so both streams re-load every iteration, the base is loop-resident in both, and the density question is live.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the four defining instructions at +0x60/+0x64/+0x8c/+0x90, both register assignments, the i/anim_base agreement at r27/r26, and the loop-body uses at +0xac/+0xc0/+0xd4/+0xd8/+0xdc were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 63-instruction body, in HEAD and in both probes.
hypothesis.statement: v1 read the boundary as 'compiler-generated temps outrank declared locals'. That reading is now too weak in one direction and too strong in the other: `count` is a DECLARED local (`s32* count;`) and it sits in the temp block at r30, while an explicitly declared `WorldInfo* wi` did not move the base out of it. So the block is decided by the web's VALUE KIND - it holds an address of a global - not by whether the programmer declared it, and not by its declared type either, since re-typing the base as u32 kept it in the block while wrecking the schedule. The untried axis is USE DENSITY inside the loop: retail's two address webs are read twice and once per iteration respectively (+0xac and +0xc0 off r29, +0xdc off r28) while the two offset webs are updated every iteration at +0xd4/+0xd8; retail ranks the frequently-UPDATED induction pair above the frequently-READ address pair and we do the reverse. A source form that changes how often the loop touches one pair - for example hoisting `gWorldInfo.worldanims` and `gWorldInfo.animdata` into the loop preheader so the base is read ONCE rather than twice per iteration - is the next probe, and it must be checked against 63/63 first, because retail demonstrably re-loads both fields every iteration and any hoist that removes those loads changes the count.
